title: Insert Interval
description:
You are given `intervals`, a list of non-overlapping `[start, end]` ranges sorted by start, and one more range `newInterval`.

Add the new range to the list, combining it with any ranges it overlaps or touches, and return a list that is still sorted and non-overlapping.

**Input format:** line 1 is `intervals` as a JSON array; line 2 is `newInterval`.

**Output format:** a JSON array of ranges.
constraints:
- 0 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
- 0 <= start <= end <= 10^5
- `intervals` is sorted by start and has no overlaps

examples.explanation: The new range bridges all three.

title: Merge Intervals
description:
Given an unsorted list of `[start, end]` ranges, combine every group of ranges that overlap or touch, and return the resulting ranges sorted by start.

**Input format:** one line, `intervals` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** a JSON array of ranges.

examples.explanation: Ranges that only share an endpoint still combine.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description:
Given a list of intervals `[start, end]`, return the **fewest** intervals you must remove so that the rest don't overlap.

Intervals that only touch, such as `[1, 2]` and `[2, 3]`, do **not** overlap here.

**Input format:** one line, `intervals` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: At most two can stay, for example [1, 2] and [3, 5], so two must go.
Three identical intervals: keep one, remove two.
Touching isn't overlapping, so nothing needs removing.

title: Meeting Rooms
description:
Each interval `[start, end]` is a meeting. Can one person attend **all** of them? That's true exactly when no two meetings overlap.

A meeting ending at time `t` does **not** clash with one starting at `t`.

**Input format:** one line, `intervals` as a JSON array (possibly empty).

**Output format:** `true` or `false`.

examples.explanation: Sorted by start: 9-10, 10-12, 13-15. Each ends before the next begins.
The second meeting starts before the first ends.
No meetings, so nothing can clash.

title: Meeting Rooms II
description:
Each interval `[start, end]` is a meeting that needs a room for its whole duration. Return the **minimum number of rooms** needed to hold every meeting.

A meeting ending at time `t` does **not** clash with one starting at `t`. So a room freed at `t` can be reused by a meeting starting at `t`.

**Input format:** one line, `intervals` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: The long meeting needs its own room; the two short ones can share another.
They don't overlap, so one room is enough.
At time 5 one room frees up exactly as another meeting starts: 2 rooms.
